column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/ansible-collection-auto-bump.yml
# TAB-separated: <name>
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS. The workflow has exactly ONE job, `bump`, with exactly
# one condition and no `needs:` graph:
#     if: github.actor != 'github-actions[bot]'
# So the entire job-selection surface is a single exact-match inequality
# against one literal actor name, and every row below is an arm of it. That
# makes the table small; it does not make it idle. `bump` COMMITS A VERSION
# BUMP TO main, PUSHES IT, PUSHES A TAG, and then dispatches release.yml on
# that tag — i.e. it is the first domino of an Ansible Galaxy publish. Whether
# it was selected or skipped is the difference between a collection version
# shipping and nothing happening, and BOTH outcomes report a green tick.
# WHY IT EXISTS. On 2026-08-08 pleme-io/graphql-synthesizer ran the sibling
# cargo-auto-release, reported SUCCESS, bumped + tagged + pushed, and published
# nothing: its `ship` job was skipped by a condition that is entirely correct.
# Nobody had written down WHICH JOBS MUST RUN for a given input, so a deliberate
# skip and a broken skip were the same green tick. Unit tests cannot see that
# (the condition is in no action's code) and actionlint cannot (the expression
# is valid). This file is that missing statement for this workflow.
# ── THE DO-IT / DON'T-DO-IT PAIR (this job publishes, so it is named out loud)
#   Row 1 is the intended DO-IT case: a non-bot actor pushed to main, so the
#   collection bumps, tags, pushes and dispatches the release.
#   Row 2 is the intended DON'T-DO-IT case, and it is the load-bearing row.
#   `bump` configures git as `github-actions[bot]` and pushes its own commit
#   under that identity. If that push re-selected this job, the workflow would
#   bump forever. This `if:` is the only thing standing between the lane and an
#   infinite self-triggered bump loop — the guard is a SINGLE line with no
#   backup, so row 2 must go red the moment it is removed, inverted, or has its
#   literal actor name edited.
# ── THE BOUNDARY ROWS, and what each would otherwise let rot ────────────────
#   Row 3 (private repo) is a TRIPWIRE, not an assertion.
#   `github.event.repository.private` appears exactly once in this workflow and
#   it is in `runs-on` — it picks a billing label (the self-hosted pool
#   for private callers, `ubuntu-latest` for public), never a job. No `if:`
#   reads it today, so row 3 must select IDENTICALLY to row 1. It is declared
#   anyway: the day someone appends `&& !github.event.repository.private` to
#   the job condition — the exact edit shape that made graphql-synthesizer ship
#   nothing while reporting success — row 3 turns NOT-RUN and the new posture
#   has to be written down rather than acquired in silence.
#   Row 4 (a different bot) pins that the guard is an EXACT-MATCH DENY OF ONE
#   IDENTITY, not a "no bots" rule. dependabot[bot], renovate and any
#   PAT-authenticated bot account DO select `bump` and DO cut a Galaxy release
#   here. That is the workflow's real behaviour, recorded as a FINDING rather
#   than discovered by a dependabot push tagging a collection. Rewriting the
#   guard as a substring or `contains()` test is a real fleet-behaviour change;
#   it turns this row red, which is the point.
#   Row 5 (empty actor) is the "the field resolved and produced NOTHING" state,
#   which is distinct from any named actor and is where guards break. Empty is
#   not the bot literal, so the job is selected — the guard FAILS OPEN. That
#   property inverts the instant the condition is rewritten as an allow-list
#   (`github.actor == 'somebody'`), an edit that reads like a hardening and
#   would silently make this lane never bump again. Row 1 would stay green;
#   row 5 is the one that catches it.
# ── WHAT THIS TABLE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT COVER ─────────────────────────────
#    (stated so nobody reads the green as broader than it is)
#   THE REAL DECISION IS A STEP, AND IT IS INVISIBLE HERE. Whether anything
#   under plugins/, meta/ or galaxy.yml changed since the previous tag is
#   computed by the `changes` step and gates the four steps that configure git,
#   bump, push and dispatch (`steps.changes.outputs.skip == 'false'`). This
#   linter models JOB selection only. "bump ran" in this table therefore means
#   "the job was selected", NEVER "a version was bumped" or "a tag was pushed":
#   a repo whose only change was a README edit selects `bump` and then
#   correctly does nothing inside it. That gap is not closable at this layer —
#   it needs a step-level oracle or a test of the `changes` script itself.
#   THE DISPATCH-OR-NOT AXIS IS UNASSERTABLE HERE. The final step is gated on
#   `steps.changes.outputs.skip == 'false' && env.HAS_BOT_PAT != 'true'`, where
#   HAS_BOT_PAT is derived from `secrets.BOT_PAT != ''`. That is a genuine
#   do-it/don't-do-it decision (with a PAT the tag push already triggered
#   release.yml, so dispatching again would duplicate the release), but it is
#   step-level AND secret-derived. Modelling it with a context key would read
#   as coverage and be none.
#   `inputs.bump-type` IS NOT A SELECTOR. It is forwarded to substrate-bump as
#   a `with:` value; no condition reads it. Neither is the BOT_PAT secret at
#   job level — it only chooses which token checkout and push use.
#   There is no type/kind dispatch and no toggle input in this workflow, so
#   there are no per-arm or catch-all rows to write. `github.actor` is the only
#   context path any condition reads, and it is the only key any row declares
#   beyond the privacy tripwire.
# 1. DO-IT. A human pushed to main; the collection bumps, commits, tags,
#    pushes, and dispatches release.yml. This is the only intended path to a
#    Galaxy publish.
human-push-bumps
# 2. DON'T-DO-IT / THE LOOP GUARD. `bump` pushes its own commit as
#    github-actions[bot]. If that push re-selected this job the workflow would
#    bump forever. This row is the reason the `if:` exists and must stay red if
#    the guard is ever removed or its literal actor name changed.
bot-push-is-the-loop-guard
# 3. TRIPWIRE (see header). A PRIVATE consumer: privacy only picks the runner
#    label, so selection is identical to row 1. If this row ever disagrees with
#    row 1, a privacy gate reached the job condition and that decision has to
#    be stated here.
private-repo-still-bumps
# 4. A DIFFERENT bot still bumps. The guard denies ONE literal identity, not
#    bots in general — pinned as a finding, not an endorsement.
other-bot-actor-still-bumps
# 5. FAIL-OPEN. Actor resolved but EMPTY — distinct from any named actor.
#    Empty != the bot literal, so `bump` is selected. Breaks loudly if the
#    guard is ever rewritten as an allow-list or a truthiness test.
empty-actor-still-bumps
